Zillow key metrics — through Q3 2026: income, segments, For Sale versus Rentals, traffic, cash, trailing PE pack from the desk series file. Latest print in file: FY2026Q3 (period end 2026-09-30).

Zillow makes money when people look for a home. Landlords and apartment managers pay to list rentals, agents pay to meet buyers, and Zillow Home Loans, the company's own mortgage lender, earns a fee on each loan it funds. In the third quarter revenue rose 7% to $724 million. Rentals did most of the work, up 26% to $220 million, with apartment-building clients up 35%. For Sale revenue, the agent and mortgage money, was flat at $489 million: agent fees fell 4%, while mortgage revenue rose 32% as home-purchase loans funded rose 55% to $1.97 billion.

The agent business is mid-switch. Two-thirds of buyers who asked to meet an agent went to a Preferred agent, who pays Zillow only when the sale closes, against about one-third a year ago. That pushes revenue later, yet over the past twelve months Zillow kept 8.8 basis points (hundredths of a percent) of the value of every U.S. home sale, up from 8.3. Zillow now filters out more automated traffic and restated its visitor counts back to 2024 on that stricter basis: 215 million monthly users, down 3%. Comscore, which measures web audiences, puts Zillow at 77% of visitors to real-estate sites, the highest it has reported.

The $158 million net loss is mostly one charge. Zillow agreed to pay $212.5 million to settle a shareholder lawsuit over its old home-buying business, expects $48 million back from insurance, and booked the $165 million difference in the quarter's administrative costs; none of it had been paid by September 30. Adjusted EBITDA, the company's profit measure before that charge, stock pay, interest, taxes and depreciation, was $182 million, 25% of revenue. Zillow ended with $707 million of cash and investments after buying back $846 million of stock this year, only $20 million of it in the third quarter. It expects fourth-quarter revenue of $635 million to $665 million, about flat on a year ago.

Risks

  • The business breaks if shoppers stop starting here and agents stop paying to meet them. The trips to watch are visits, which means how many times people open the site and the apps; average monthly unique users, which means how many different people show up in a typical month; and the audience share the company quotes.
  • The mortgage line moves with rates and with how many loans Zillow Home Loans actually funds.
  • Another portal can take the agent dollar. That shows up on the For Sale line.
  • Rentals stops compounding, or the listings the site depends on get pulled.

Close competitors

  • Redfin — a brokerage with its own site, so it both sends shoppers and competes for the agent.
  • Homes.com (CoStar) — a portal built to sell agents the same kind of advertising.
  • Realtor.com — the other large listings site shoppers already know.
  • Compass — a brokerage that can keep its agents off a portal.
  • Opendoor — buys houses, which is the model Zillow left.

Unit economics, data access, and how the company is run are written up separately, and this page does not repeat them.

Open gaps

  1. There is no forward earnings multiple for next fiscal year, because no analyst estimate has been locked yet. The buy box stays on hold, and no street multiple is drawn. The forward-valuation dig is not live yet, so there is no link to it.
  2. The trailing multiple is blank from 2026 week 40 through week 45. Trailing twelve-month net income is negative, $3M + $46M − $4M − $158M = −$113M (calculated), and the house counts a quarter from the first week after it ends. Those weeks keep their prices. The last printed multiple is 132.7× in 2026 week 39.
  3. The 2026 week 45 price, $31.45, is calculated as the volume-weighted average of Nasdaq's public daily closes for November 2–6. Earlier weeks come from the house weekly price file.
  4. Weekly price and the trailing multiple start at 2020 week 31 because that is the first week in the file. Earlier weeks were not invented.
  5. Visits and average monthly unique users on the old measure end at the second quarter of 2026; the company no longer prints them. The stricter measure starts at the first quarter of 2024, the earliest quarter the company restated, and the two are not joined.
  6. Average monthly unique users on the old measure is blank at FY2015Q4, FY2016Q4, FY2017Q4, FY2018Q4, FY2019Q4, FY2020Q4, FY2021Q4, and FY2022Q4. Visits are blank before FY2017 and at FY2017Q4, FY2018Q4, FY2019Q4, FY2020Q4, and FY2021Q4. FY2022Q4 visits are printed.
  7. For Sale revenue per dollar of home sales starts at the third quarter of 2025. Earlier quarters were printed on an older way of counting home-sale value, which put the figure about a fifth higher, so they are left off rather than mixed in.
  8. Quarterly operating cash flow and adjusted free cash flow start at the third quarter of 2025. Earlier quarters are in earlier releases and were not extracted for this page.
  9. Employee counts come from annual reports only. Quarterly reports do not print one, so the third quarter of 2026 is blank; the company announced a cut of about 7% of staff in August. Years before 2021 were not extracted for this page.
  10. Comscore share is carried from the first quarter of 2026. Earlier quarters were not extracted for this page. The share of buyer connections going to Preferred agents is printed only as "two-thirds" this quarter and is not charted.
  11. Home-purchase loans funded are blank at the fourth quarter of 2022 and before 2022; those were not extracted. Other fourth quarters are the year less the first three quarters, marked derived.
  12. Net income, operating income and earnings per share versus the year before are blank for the third quarter of 2026. A year earlier net income was a small profit and operating income a small loss, so a percent change would mislead.
  13. The company now reports first-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA as $198 million, after moving Federal Trade Commission litigation costs out of the measure. The page keeps the $182 million first printed.
  14. Revenue CAGR 4.9% for FY2021–FY2025 is already on the annual income chart, labeled derived. Operating income and net income have no CAGR on that window because the endpoints are not both positive. Do not run a longer CAGR across FY2019 into FY2020.
  15. Free cash flow is not a line in the annual reports. The annual page charts operating cash flow and the two capex cash lines instead. There is no single printed capex total.
  16. Operating income and net income by Residential, Mortgages, and Rentals are not disclosed.
  17. Annual history starts at FY2013. Current Residential, Mortgages, and Rentals lines start in FY2021 annual and FY2023Q1 quarterly; older labels were not spliced onto them.
  18. Adjusted EBITDA versus the year before is blank at FY2023Q4. The year-before quarter is printed as zero, so a percent is undefined.
